elasticsearch.EntryDispatched.answers: confirms an entry step was dispatched — the first record in a run's ledger
elasticsearch.EntryDispatched.never_for: current state — ES is history; and identifying a run by WorkflowId alone — the control plane's own start/stop log lines carry WorkflowId too, so filter on this template as well

elasticsearch.HandoffDispatched.answers: confirms a hand-off was dispatched, with its elapsed ms
elasticsearch.HandoffDispatched.never_for: current state — ES is history; a WorkflowId filter alone cannot identify a run, because the control-plane endpoints log it too

elasticsearch.RunningTheStep.never_for: current state — ES is history; a WorkflowId filter alone cannot identify a run, because the control-plane endpoints log it too

elasticsearch.AuthorConfig.answers: the config values (Label, Number) a step actually ran with, as logged at execution time
elasticsearch.AuthorConfig.never_for: current state — ES is history; and the config schema itself — that is the processor's ConfigSchemaId in Postgres, not this record

elasticsearch.StepReturned.answers: confirms a step returned, with elapsed ms — a per-event figure worth trusting over an interpolated histogram quantile at coarse resolution
elasticsearch.StepReturned.never_for: current state — ES is history; a WorkflowId filter alone cannot identify a run, because the control-plane endpoints log it too

elasticsearch.BranchCompleted.answers: confirms a branch completed, with elapsed ms
elasticsearch.BranchCompleted.never_for: current state — ES is history; a WorkflowId filter alone cannot identify a run, because the control-plane endpoints log it too

elasticsearch.EntryStepCompleted.answers: confirms the entry step completed, carrying its Result
elasticsearch.EntryStepCompleted.never_for: current state — ES is history; a WorkflowId filter alone cannot identify a run, because the control-plane endpoints log it too

elasticsearch.HandedOff.answers: one hand-off's NextStepId, NextProcessorId and NextEntryId
elasticsearch.HandedOff.never_for: current state — ES is history; a WorkflowId filter alone cannot identify a run, because the control-plane endpoints log it too

elasticsearch.AdvancedSuccessors.answers: confirms N successors were advanced, with elapsed ms — the fan-out width and its cost
elasticsearch.AdvancedSuccessors.never_for: current state — ES is history; a WorkflowId filter alone cannot identify a run, because the control-plane endpoints log it too

elasticsearch.TerminalCompleted.answers: confirms a run reached a terminal step with no successor — the ledger's last record, used to confirm a run actually finished
elasticsearch.TerminalCompleted.never_for: current state — ES is history; a WorkflowId filter alone cannot identify a run, because the control-plane endpoints log it too

elasticsearch.EntryAbsentDuplicate.answers: explains a short ledger as a benign duplicate delivery of the entry step rather than a lost step
elasticsearch.EntryAbsentDuplicate.never_for: evidence that something is broken — this is the legitimate excuse for why nothing else in the ledger was logged

elasticsearch.EntryDispatchSendFailed.answers: the entry-step dispatch failed to send, but the handler continued rather than crash
elasticsearch.EntryDispatchSendFailed.never_for: assuming the run proceeded unaffected — the dispatch genuinely failed to send

elasticsearch.StoreUnreachable.answers: the projection store was unreachable and the message was returned to its queue — logged above the deserialization boundary
elasticsearch.StoreUnreachable.never_for: attributing this to one run by WorkflowId — at this point in the code the ids are still undecoded bytes; it only witnesses the fault window, not a specific run

elasticsearch.RefusingAndParking.answers: a message was rejected and the broker confirmed the park — it is now recoverable from the queue's Dead sibling
elasticsearch.RefusingAndParking.never_for: attributing this to one run by WorkflowId — the ids are still undecoded bytes at this point in the code

elasticsearch.RefusingNotParked.answers: a message was rejected but the channel died before the broker heard it — it will be REDELIVERED, not dead-lettered
elasticsearch.RefusingNotParked.never_for: looking for this message in a dead-letter queue — it is not there, and the rabbitmq.*Dead surfaces will not show it

elasticsearch.SendFailedReturning.answers: a send failed while handling a message and it was returned to its queue
elasticsearch.SendFailedReturning.never_for: attributing this to one run by WorkflowId — the ids are still undecoded bytes at this point in the code

elasticsearch.GateClosed.answers: the L2 gate closed on this host — projection store unusable, consumers paused; pair with GateOpen to measure one outage's duration
elasticsearch.GateClosed.never_for: the gate's live state — that is prometheus.pipeline_gate_open; this is only a historical transition record

elasticsearch.GateOpen.answers: the L2 gate reopened — projection store healthy again; pair with GateClosed to measure one outage's duration
elasticsearch.GateOpen.never_for: the gate's live state — that is prometheus.pipeline_gate_open; this is only a historical transition record

elasticsearch.ChannelShutDown.answers: the AMQP channel shut down for a stated reason and will reopen
elasticsearch.ChannelShutDown.never_for: current state — ES is history; the channel may already have reopened by the time this is read

elasticsearch.ConnectionRecovered.answers: the AMQP connection recovered; delivery tags issued before this point are invalid
elasticsearch.ConnectionRecovered.never_for: current state — ES is history, this only confirms a past recovery happened

elasticsearch.ConsumptionPaused.answers: consumption stopped, naming the queue, because it is no longer admitted or the store is unhealthy
elasticsearch.ConsumptionPaused.never_for: current consuming state — that is pipeline.queue.consumers in Prometheus; this is a historical transition

elasticsearch.ConsumptionAdmitted.answers: consumption resumed, naming the queue, because it is admitted and the store is healthy
elasticsearch.ConsumptionAdmitted.never_for: current consuming state — that is pipeline.queue.consumers in Prometheus; this only confirms a past resumption happened

elasticsearch.HostShuttingDown.answers: a host is shutting down — emitted by Microsoft.Hosting.Lifetime, so every service in the deployment writes this exact line
elasticsearch.HostShuttingDown.never_for: identifying which role shut down from this template alone — every service writes it; filter on the service name too, or use a role-unique template instead

elasticsearch.ProcessorLoopsRetired.answers: this processor's startup loops stood down because it is now healthy and serving — processor-unique
elasticsearch.ProcessorLoopsRetired.never_for: any other role's startup — this template is written only by a processor

elasticsearch.SchedulerShuttingDown.answers: the Quartz scheduler is shutting down — orchestrator-unique, Quartz runs nowhere else in this deployment
elasticsearch.SchedulerShuttingDown.never_for: any other role's shutdown — this template names the scheduler, which only the orchestrator runs

elasticsearch.OrchestratorHydrated.answers: the orchestrator finished hydrating WorkflowCount workflows from L2 and is admitting its consumer — orchestrator-unique, no other role writes it
elasticsearch.OrchestratorHydrated.never_for: a processor's own readiness — that is elasticsearch.ProcessorLoopsRetired or prometheus.pipeline_identity_ready

elasticsearch.index.answers: which data stream every other elasticsearch.* surface and elasticsearch.attr.* field is actually read from -- logs-generic.otel-default, ~10.08 million documents as of 2026-08-30 and growing continuously on a shared cluster
elasticsearch.index.never_for: an unbounded query -- always bound on time and workflow (see the Elastic class docstring); this is not a small lookup table, it is the whole run history
